name: UNICEF USA
mission: Over eight decades, the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) has built an unprecedented global support system for the world's children. UNICEF relentlessly works day in and day out to deliver the essentials that give every child an equitable chance in life: health care and immunizations, safe water and sanitation, nutrition, education, emergency relief and more. UNICEF USA advances the global mission of UNICEF by rallying the American public to support the world's most vulnerable children. Together, we have helped save more children's lives than any other humanitarian organization.
theoryOfChange: UNICEF USA, through its Impact Fund for Children, has co-developed a 'Child-Lens Investment Framework'. This framework serves as a roadmap for investors to frame strategies and direct capital toward advancing child outcomes and minimizing child harm. It is described as a 'central guiding document' that includes core principles, a case for investment, an analysis of the global market landscape, and a description of the Child-Lens Investment ecosystem. Additionally, the Impact Fund reports impact through an 'Input/Output/Outcomes Framework' and by mapping each acceleration to UNICEF to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

strengths_deep_dive: UNICEF USA excels in organizational governance and transparency. They maintain a <cite id="13">board of 21 members</cite>, ensuring diverse oversight for their massive global operations. Their commitment to data is evidenced by <cite id="14">tracking 3 distinct outcome metrics</cite> through Candid, which is rare for organizations of this size. Furthermore, they maintain <cite id="15">2.8 months of working capital</cite>, providing a stable financial cushion for long-term projects despite recent revenue fluctuations.
rich_narrative.summary: UNICEF USA operates as a major humanitarian force dedicated to child survival and health across more than 190 countries. The organization reported <cite id="1">total revenue of $829,050,932</cite> in FY2025, primarily driven by <cite id="2">$825,269,573 in public contributions</cite>. Their work spans critical sectors including nutrition, water, and sanitation. While the organization maintains a <cite id="3">97/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite>, recent financial data shows a transition period. Revenue <cite id="4">declined 13% in the most recent fiscal year</cite>, moving from over $829 million to $720,404,955. Despite this contraction, the charity remains a massive grantmaker. They distributed <cite id="5">$989,277,560 in total grants</cite> in FY2025, with the vast majority of <cite id="6">$961,292,120 directed to foreign recipients</cite>. This scale allows them to address systemic issues like child mortality, which <cite id="7">improved in 33 countries</cite> according to recent research. However, the organization faces challenges in maintaining its historical spending efficiency. The <cite id="8">program expense ratio is 85.7%</cite> according to FY2025 filings, which is significantly lower than the <cite id="9">peer program ratio median of 82.9%</cite>. This gap suggests that a larger portion of funds is currently being utilized for administrative and fundraising infrastructure compared to similar humanitarian peers.
